title: Stuffed Corn Griddle Cakes with Refried Beans, Cheese and Cabbage Relish
summary: These corn masa cakes hide a creamy mashed pinto bean and melted cheese filling, griddled until crisp and spotted brown. They're served warm with a quick tangy cabbage relish and a simple tomato salsa for balance.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper
large heavy frying pan or griddle, preferably cast iron

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
boiling water, plus extra warm water as needed
neutral oil, plus extra for the pan
can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the curtido
steps.text: Combine the cabbage, carrot, onion, oregano, vinegar, water and the 1/4 tsp salt in a bowl, pressing down on the cabbage so it bruises and starts to release liquid. Set aside for at least 30 minutes, giving it an occasional stir, so it has time to soften and pick up the sharp, tangy flavour of the vinegar. Make this first, since curtido only improves the longer it sits while you prepare everything else.

steps.title: Simmer the tomato salsa
steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and jalapeño to a smooth purée. Heat the oil in a small saucepan over medium heat, pour in the purée (it will spit, so stand back a little) and stir in the 1/4 tsp salt, then simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly. Simmering briefly mellows the sharpness of the raw tomato and tightens the sauce so it clings rather than running off the pupusas.

steps.title: Cook the bean filling
steps.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat, add the garlic and cumin and stir for about 30 seconds until fragrant; this short toast in hot oil wakes up the spice's flavour before the beans go in. Add the beans and water and mash everything well with a potato masher, cooking for 4-5 minutes until you have a thick paste that holds its shape on a spoon rather than slumping. Spread the mash out on a plate and leave to cool for 10 minutes, then mix in the mozzarella and divide into 8 balls of about 50g each. Wipe out the pan ready for cooking the pupusas later.

steps.title: Mix and rest the dough
steps.text: Stir the masa harina and 1/4 tsp salt together, then add the boiling water and 1 tsp oil and mix with a spatula to a soft dough. Cover and leave to rest for 20 minutes so the corn flour hydrates fully and the dough firms up enough to handle. Knead briefly for 15-20 seconds, then flatten a small piece to test it: if the edges crack more than a few millimetres, work in warm water a teaspoon at a time until it feels soft and slightly tacky, like play dough. Divide into 8 balls of about 85g each and keep them under a damp tea towel so they don't dry out while you shape the rest.

steps.title: Fill and shape the pupusas
steps.text: Using moistened hands, push your thumb firmly into a dough ball to form a deep hollow, then shape the sides into a small corn-dough bowl with walls roughly 6mm thick. Drop in a portion of the bean and cheese filling, pull the dough up over it and pinch firmly to seal, then roll gently back into a ball. Pat it out between your palms into a disc about 10cm wide and 1.5cm thick, smoothing any cracks with a wet finger so the filling stays sealed in as it heats through. Place it on the lined tray under the damp towel and repeat with the rest.

steps.title: Griddle until golden
steps.text: Place the heavy frying pan over medium heat and lightly rub the surface with a touch of oil before the pupusas go on. Working in batches so the pan isn't crowded, cook the pupusas for about 4 minutes per side, until they're browned in spots, crisp at the edges and the cheese inside has melted through. Drain briefly on kitchen paper and serve hot, with the curtido and tomato salsa on the side, while the cheese is still soft.

tips: Mash the beans until they hold their shape on a spoon - a runny filling is the most common reason pupusas burst open on the griddle, so cook off enough water to get a stiff paste.
Use the crack test on the dough before you start filling: a piece that crumbles at the edges needs a little more warm water kneaded in.
Cool the bean mixture before mixing in the cheese, or the cheese will start to melt and make the filling too soft to shape.
Keep the pan at medium heat rather than high, so the masa cooks through and the cheese melts before the outside scorches.
Give the curtido the full resting time, or make it the day before - it keeps well and the flavour deepens overnight in the fridge.
storage: Refrigerate cooked pupusas within 1 hour and use within 3 days; reheat in a dry pan over medium-low heat until piping hot (74°C) throughout. The curtido keeps in the fridge for up to 1 week in a covered container. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
